topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text: The edge of familiar ground shifts, blurring where the known ends and the wild begins. Paw prints overlap, a dance of claim and yield. The air, laced with the scent of another, lingers where it should not. A presence, deliberate and different, treads softly near the bounds I guard. They speak in gestures, their hands stretching toward the soil as if to form a pact with the earth itself. I watch, muscles coiled, as they propose a reshaping of the land. Roots will dig, leaves will spread, and the space will bear the mark of their touch. The balance shifts, and with it, the rhythm of the territory alters, inviting a new dance of coexistence.
